| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| `query` | string | Yes | — | Search query text. Max 5,000 characters. Supports search operators like `site:` and `filetype:`. |
| `location` | string | No | — | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for region-specific results (e.g., `"US"`, `"GB"`, `"JP"`). |
| `sources` | string\[] | No | — | Sources to query: `web`, `news`, `scholar-articles`, `scholar-articles-enriched`, `scholar-author`, `ai`, `social`. Omitting this field searches all sources. |
| `site` | string | No | — | Restrict results to a domain (e.g., `"linkedin.com/company"`, `"github.com"`). Max 500 characters. |
| `start_date` | integer | No | — | Unix timestamp (seconds). Only results after this date. |
| `end_date` | integer | No | — | Unix timestamp (seconds). Only results before this date. Must be > `start_date`. |
| `human_mode` | boolean | No | `false` | Attempt a browser-like retrieval path when standard search access is blocked by bot protection. |
| `page` | integer | No | `1` | Number of result pages to aggregate into the response. Minimum `1`, maximum `15`. Values above `15` return `400`. When `page` is greater than `1`, `sources` must contain exactly one source. |
<Snippet file="web-site-parameter.mdx" />
***
## Response fields reference
| Field | Type | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `success` | boolean | Whether the search executed successfully. |
| `query` | string | The query as interpreted by the API (includes `site:` prefix if `site` was set). |
| `timestamp` | integer | Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the search was performed. |
| `results` | array | Search results. Shape varies by `source` — see [Sources](#sources). |
| `metadata.total_results` | integer | Total number of results available across all pages (may exceed the number in the `results` array if you requested fewer pages). |
| `metadata.failed_pages` | array | Page numbers that failed to return results. |
| `metadata.empty_pages` | array | Page numbers that returned no results. |
<Note>
  **Timestamps:** Search `timestamp` is in **milliseconds**. Fetch `timestamp`
  is in **seconds**. Divide Search timestamps by 1000 when comparing across
  endpoints.
</Note>
***
## Error handling
Search returns `400` for invalid requests and `401` for auth failures.
<CodeGroup>
  ```json 400 — missing query theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
  {
      "error": {
          "type": "invalid_request",
          "message": "query: This field is required.",
          "metadata": []
      }
  }
  ```
  ```json 400 — invalid source theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
  {
      "error": {
          "type": "invalid_request",
          "message": "sources: {0: [ErrorDetail(string='\"invalid_source\" is not a valid choice.', code='invalid_choice')]}",
          "metadata": []
      }
  }
  ```
  ```json 401 — bad API key theme={"theme":"vitesse-black"}
  {
      "message": "Invalid API key in request"
  }
  ```
</CodeGroup>
<Snippet file="web-error-responses.mdx" />
***
## Common gotchas
| Mistake | Fix |
| - | - |
| Omitting `sources` and expecting uniform results | Different sources return different fields. Specify `sources` explicitly for predictable parsing. |
| Using `site` with `scholar-author` or `ai` sources | `site` only applies to `web` and `news` sources. It has no effect on academic or deep research searches. |
| Expecting `snippet` in deep research mode results | Deep research mode returns `content` and `references` instead of `snippet` and `position`. |
| Expecting `position` in scholar-author results | Academic author results don't have `position` — they have `name`, `affiliation`, `citations`, etc. |
| Using `start_date` >= `end_date` | `start_date` must be strictly less than `end_date`. |
***
## API reference summary
| Detail | Value |
| - | - |
| **Endpoint** | `POST /web/search/live` |
| **Auth** | Bearer token + `x-api-version: 2025-11-01` |
| **Pricing** | `1 credit per query` |
| **Request** | `query` (required). Optional: `location`, `sources`, `site`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `human_mode`, `page`. |
| **Response** | Object: `{ success, query, timestamp, results[], metadata }` |
| **Errors** | `400` (bad request), `401` (bad auth) |
See the [full API reference](/openapi-specs/2025-11-01/introduction) for
the complete OpenAPI schema.

## Crustdata payloads are now capped at the request, and "search about zepto" completes

The overflow is fixed by asking Crustdata only for the fields the agent needs. Market Researcher's "search about zepto" now finishes normally. The commit is **`8ba766a`** `fix(tools): cap crustdata payloads with api-side field filters`, pushed to `origin/worktree-web-ui-scaffold` (05113c0..8ba766a). It changes `src/mastra/tools/crustdata.ts` and `src/mastra/prompts/index.ts`.

I re-read CLAUDE.md, spawned no subagents and worked only in the worktree. `src/telemetry.ts` is still untracked and not committed, and `whatsapp.ts` was not touched. Root `tsc` passes.

### Root cause
A single old enrich call for zeptonow.com returned **5,063,646 bytes, about 1.27M tokens**, which alone is over DeepSeek's 1,048,576-token limit.
- 4.53 MB of that was `people.decision_makers`: 300 full profiles.
- `people.cxos` (27 profiles) was 366 KB and `people.founders` (21) was 64 KB.
- `headcount.by_function_timeseries` (40 KB) and `funding.milestones` (30 KB) made up most of the rest.

### What the docs say
- **Enrich** ([reference](https://docs.crustdata.com/company-docs/enrichment/reference.md), [introduction](https://docs.crustdata.com/company-docs/enrichment/introduction.md), [API reference](https://docs.crustdata.com/api-reference/company-apis/get-full-company-enrichment.md)):
  - `fields` takes section names, and the introduction confirms dot-path subfields work: only that subfield is filled in and its siblings come back as `null`.
  - I confirmed in a real call that paths into array items also work (`people.founders.basic_profile.name`).
  - There is no match-count parameter and no per-list limit (people, news); only `exact_match`.
- **Search** ([reference](https://docs.crustdata.com/company-docs/search/reference.md), [introduction](https://docs.crustdata.com/company-docs/search/introduction.md)):
  - Ranked-search `limit` is 1–100 (default 20). `fields` takes dot paths; leaving it out returns everything.
  - The response is `{ companies, next_cursor, total_count }`, which our code already read correctly (confirmed live).
  - `basic_info.description` isn't in the documented field list but is returned in practice (confirmed live).
- **Web Search** ([reference](https://docs.crustdata.com/web-docs/search/reference.md)):
  - There is **no result-count parameter**. `page` (minimum 1, default 1) is the only size control; `sources`, `site` and `start_date`/`end_date` only narrow the scope.
- **Headers** ([best practices](https://docs.crustdata.com/openapi-specs/2025-11-01/best-practices.md)): only rate-limit response headers; no request header affects payload size.

### Per-tool request changes
- **`crustdataCompanyEnrich`**
  - The coarse section list is replaced by dot-path fields:
    - `basic_info` and `locations.headquarters`
    - `headcount.total`, `headcount.growth_percent`, `headcount.largest_headcount_country`
    - `funding.total_investment_usd`, `last_round_amount_usd`, `last_round_type`, `last_fundraise_date`, `num_funding_rounds`, `investors`
    - `competitors.all_domains`, `competitors.organic_seo`
  - A simple opt-in `extras` input, each narrowed the same way:
    - `people`: founders and CXOs, `basic_profile.name` and `current_title` only
    - `news`: title, url and date
    - `revenue`, `hiring`, `taxonomy`
  - `decision_makers`, timeseries and milestones are never requested.
  - Only the best match is kept. That picks which company to use; the API has no match limit.
- **`crustdataCompanySearch`:** default `limit` lowered from 10 to 5 (max 25), with the same dot-path `fields` and the `companies` envelope.
- **`crustdataWebSearch`:** now sends `page: 1` explicitly. The existing 10-result `slice` is still there because the API has no count parameter.
- **Last-resort guard:** a clearly commented 150 KB check per tool. If a result is still over that, the model gets a short "too large, narrow your request" message instead of the data. The real cap is the field selection.
- **Prompt:** call enrich once, add extras only when the task needs them, prefer web search (news source) for recent news, keep search limits small, and plan one or two calls before firing more.

### Sizes for Zepto (real calls: 3 before, 3 after)
| Tool | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| enrich | 5,063,646 B (~1.27M tok) | 51,292 B (~12.8K tok) with people + news; core profile ≈ 4.8 KB |
| search | 8,159 B (10 rows) | 5,352 B (5 rows) |
| web | 3,814 B | 3,546 B |

Within the 51 KB enrich result: people is 16.4 KB (48 names and titles, with null placeholder keys) and news is 30 KB (100 articles).

The core-only figure comes from the per-section sizes in that same response, to stay within the call budget. The end-to-end run below then used 4 more calls (1 enrich, 3 web).

### End-to-end
I sent "search about zepto" to `/api/chat/market-researcher` through the running server (curl).
- The agent made 4 tool calls: enrich with all five extras, plus three web searches.
- Tool output totalled **65.5 KB (about 16K tokens)**, compared with about 1.33M before.
- The stream ended with `finish` and `finishReason: "stop"`.
- The server log had no "oversized" span message and no errors.
- The server is stopped.

### What the API can't cap
- **Enrich `news`** always returns up to 100 articles (30 KB for Zepto). It's opt-in, and the prompt steers the agent to web search instead, whose result size is fixed by `page: 1`.
- **Enrich lists in general** (founders, CXOs, investors, competitor domains) have no count limit. Requesting only the needed subfields keeps them small: 48 people came to 16 KB.
- **Web Search** has no count parameter, so the 10-result selection stays.

One thing to watch: in the end-to-end run the agent asked for all five extras on its first enrich call despite the prompt. The result was still small (54 KB), but you may want to tune the prompt further if credits matter.

  - A simple opt-in `extras` input, each narrowed the same way:
    - `people`: founders and CXOs, `basic_profile.name` and `current_title` only
    - `news`: title, url and date
    - `revenue`, `hiring`, `taxonomy`
  - `decision_makers`, timeseries and milestones are never requested.
  - Only the best match is kept. That picks which company to use; the API has no match limit.
- **`crustdataCompanySearch`:** default `limit` lowered from 10 to 5 (max 25), with the same dot-path `fields` and the `companies` envelope.
- **`crustdataWebSearch`:** now sends `page: 1` explicitly. The existing 10-result `slice` is still there because the API has no count parameter.
- **Last-resort guard:** a clearly commented 150 KB check per tool. If a result is still over that, the model gets a short "too large, narrow your request" message instead of the data. The real cap is the field selection.
- **Prompt:** call enrich once, add extras only when the task needs them, prefer web search (news source) for recent news, keep search limits small, and plan one or two calls before firing more.

### Sizes for Zepto (real calls: 3 before, 3 after)
| Tool | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| enrich | 5,063,646 B (~1.27M tok) | 51,292 B (~12.8K tok) with people + news; core profile ≈ 4.8 KB |
| search | 8,159 B (10 rows) | 5,352 B (5 rows) |
| web | 3,814 B | 3,546 B |

Within the 51 KB enrich result: people is 16.4 KB (48 names and titles, with null placeholder keys) and news is 30 KB (100 articles).

The core-only figure comes from the per-section sizes in that same response, to stay within the call budget. The end-to-end run below then used 4 more calls (1 enrich, 3 web).

### End-to-end
I sent "search about zepto" to `/api/chat/market-researcher` through the running server (curl).
- The agent made 4 tool calls: enrich with all five extras, plus three web searches.
- Tool output totalled **65.5 KB (about 16K tokens)**, compared with about 1.33M before.
- The stream ended with `finish` and `finishReason: "stop"`.
- The server log had no "oversized" span message and no errors.
- The server is stopped.

### What the API can't cap
- **Enrich `news`** always returns up to 100 articles (30 KB for Zepto). It's opt-in, and the prompt steers the agent to web search instead, whose result size is fixed by `page: 1`.
- **Enrich lists in general** (founders, CXOs, investors, competitor domains) have no count limit. Requesting only the needed subfields keeps them small: 48 people came to 16 KB.
- **Web Search** has no count parameter, so the 10-result selection stays.

One thing to watch: in the end-to-end run the agent asked for all five extras on its first enrich call despite the prompt. The result was still small (54 KB), but you may want to tune the prompt further if credits matter.
